A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same TOPBENCH study. All 35 pages, including figures, tables, equations, and Appendices A–E, support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original model evaluations, semantic-information and predict-only ablations, judge audits, and supplementary analyses in Sections 5–6 and the appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results, including the model comparison in Table 2 and ablations in Tables 3–4.

M1.justification: The dataset-construction pipeline, intent-to-prediction formulation, text-based and ReAct workflows, and predict-only ensemble remain unchanged. The broader agentic applicability stated in Section 5.1 was already demonstrated in v1's Table 2.

E1.justification: Both versions use 779 queries from 35 source tables across the same four tasks and three domains. Appendix B.1 corrects descriptive counts without establishing a change to the underlying coverage.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged in the text-based, agentic, semantic-information, and predict-only comparisons. Newly cited related works are not added experimental baselines.

E3.justification: Section 4.2 now specifies batch NMAE with each normalized absolute error capped at 1.0 before averaging. v1 described averaging NMAE and supplied an uncapped base definition in Appendix C.3. This revises the reported scoring specification; the PDFs do not establish that evaluation was rerun.

E4.justification: The semantic-information and predict-only ablations, truncation comparisons, judge robustness checks, metric sensitivity study, tool-use analyses, and qualitative cases are retained without changed evidence.

E5.justification: Repeated-run, seed, and statistical uncertainty reporting are unchanged. Neither version adds uncertainty estimates or significance tests for aggregate performance; the existing audit and judge-agreement reporting is retained.

E6.justification: Reported performance values and rankings are unchanged. Appendix B.1 replaces 17 short, 17 medium, and 183 long-list queries with 34 short and 180 long-list queries, correcting the long-list share from approximately 68% to 84% and reconciling the counts with the retained total of 214.

T1.justification: New Equation 3 explicitly defines clipped batch NMAE, bounding each normalized error contribution at 1.0, beyond v1's uncapped NMAE definition and verbal averaging rule. Other mathematical content is unchanged; replacing the width-penalty symbol tau with kappa is only notation.

C1.justification: The benchmark contribution and conclusions about intent recognition and predictive precision retain their scientific scope. Replacing promotional phrases such as 'new standard' and 'shifts the paradigm' with more restrained wording does not change those claims.

C2.justification: The revised conclusion explains more explicitly why paired historical tables isolate predictive reasoning from data-search failures. That isolation rationale and the limitation concerning open-ended data discovery were already stated in v1; substantive result interpretations and failure mechanisms remain unchanged.

D1.justification: The explicit 1.0 clipping rule supplies additional information for reproducing batch-NMAE scoring. Repository access, prompt templates, judge configuration, model identifiers, and execution setup remain unchanged.

R1.justification: Sections 2.2–2.3 add seven cited works, including TabFSBench and VT-Bench, without substantially rewriting the research positioning. Several additions have apparently mismatched relevance: their listed titles concern waveguide filters, TSN network timing, or graph-inference encryption. Other changes largely update bibliographic metadata for existing works.

P1.justification: v2 revises the title, corrects terminology and grammar, expands evaluation and conclusion wording, and updates the publication footer and bibliography. The section organization and most prose remain intact.

P2.justification: Figure 1 receives wording, example-cell, and sizing corrections. Figure 3 changes 'Medical' to 'Healthcare' and moves earlier; Figure 5 and Tables 3–4 are repositioned. The underlying plots, table structures, and appendix displays are otherwise retained.

improvement.justification: v2 fixes internally inconsistent candidate counts and makes batch-error clipping explicit, improving reporting clarity. However, newly added citations include apparently unrelated waveguide-filter and network-timing papers as support for TQA positioning. With unchanged experimental evidence and these competing gains and relevance problems, the PDFs do not establish a reliable net direction in overall quality.
